GARDENER MOUSE: Gardener Mouse, ONE honey-brown clay mouse (brown, not grey) standing upright on two legs, with big round peach-pink ears, a pink nose, rosy cheeks, a long thin pink tail, a wide floppy straw sun hat with one white daisy tucked in its band, green overalls (dungarees) with one big front pocket over a cream shirt, and little brown boots; a little taller than Echo. DUCKS: two friendly clay ducks, always the same two: a mallard with a glossy green head, a thin white neck ring and a soft grey-brown body, and a speckled light-brown duck; both with orange bills and orange webbed feet; each about as tall as Echo. FROG: one little round leaf-green clay pond frog (a real frog, not a toy: no wind-up key) with a few darker green spots on its back, big golden eyes, a pale cream tummy and a wide happy smile; about half Echo's height. The place in this story is Gardener Mouse's garden on a sunny green hillside: sandy paths, low wooden beds of herbs, little seedlings, berry bushes and flowers, a white picket fence, a little stone spring near the top of the garden with a small wooden gate in front of it, a big chunky wooden waterwheel near the spring, a little wooden water tank on legs beside the wheel, open wooden water troughs (long wooden channels shaped like little slides, each with a U-shaped groove down its middle) and a small round stone-edged pond lower down the hill. Until the ending pages, no water runs anywhere at all; the spring's little wooden gate is shut, the stone spring basin is still, the wheel is dry and still, every trough is empty and dry, the pond is an empty bowl of dry pebbles, and the flowers droop; never draw a waterfall, a stream, a trickle or a splash on a page before the ending.
